subject: Cutover buffer proposal for Acme MAP
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Cutover buffer proposal for Acme MAP

Team —

Quick planning note before I loop Acme in tomorrow: Acme's MAP currently targets a go‑live of 2027‑07‑01. Procurement has been slow on the legal side (see last week), and the evaluation window is still running longer than we expected. I think we should proactively offer a small cutover buffer and a refined contingency so the customer has a clear, low‑friction path if internal approvals slide.

Proposal (high level):
- Offer a two‑week cutover buffer to 2027‑07‑15 as an option (no charge change) if they submit procurement signals by 6/29.
- Include a short MAP addendum with explicit acceptance criteria for evaluation (three smoke tests + latency signoff) to unblock the final procurement milestone.
- Prepare a limited credit (2 weeks of discounted overage protection) as a goodwill gesture if we need to extend beyond 7/15 due to procurement lag.

I attached a draft of the MAP addendum and a working risk log (local copy) for reference. If you all agree, I'll send a concise note to Sofia with the buffer + contingency details and attach the MAP addendum. Marcus — can you validate the capacity language? Laura — can you confirm legal is OK with the two‑week buffer clause? Rishi — heads up on the pricing credit mechanics if we need to route for approval.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415‑555‑0191

Attachment stubs: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf, close_risk_log.xlsx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Cutover buffer proposal for Acme MAP

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for a productive eval call yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a short, written proposal on the table so your stakeholders (procurement/legal/IT) have a low‑friction option if approvals run late. We want to make sure you can complete testing and avoid a rushed cutover.

Proposal summary:
- Primary target: 2027‑07‑01 (as currently in the MAP).
- Option A (buffer): move to 2027‑07‑15 with the same commercial terms if procurement provides signed signals by 2027‑06‑29.
- Contingency: if procurement extends past 7/15 through no fault of your evaluation team, we will offer 2 weeks of discounted overage protection (details in attached MAP addendum) to cover initial traffic variance during ramp.

Acceptance criteria for cutover (to be signed off by your evaluation owner):
1) Three smoke tests passing: basic generation, streaming latency within SLO, embeddings correctness sample
2) Security checklist complete (SOC2 items confirmed)
3) Integration runbook handed to your ops team

Attached: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf (draft addendum), close_risk_log.xlsx (internal risk register). If this looks reasonable, can you confirm whether procurement would accept the 6/29 signal cutoff? If procurement needs a different trigger, we can adjust.

Happy to jump on a 15‑minute call with procurement/legal if helpful.

Best,
Naomi

Attachment stubs: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf, close_risk_log.xlsx
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover buffer proposal for Acme MAP

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear summary and the addendum. Two quick notes from our side:
1) Procurement says the earliest they can deliver a signed PO is the week of 7/5 (legal availability, internal budget approvals). They cannot commit to 6/29.
2) Our evaluation team would prefer not to shorten the testing window — they want to keep the current schedule and would rather push cutover than compress tests.

Given the procurement timing, we are asking whether you can accommodate a cutover of 2027‑07‑22 (three weeks later) without changing the quoted pricing. We understand if that requires special approval. Also, we would like the MAP addendum to explicitly state the conditions that trigger the contested credit — procurement wants clear, simple language.

Can you advise next steps?

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
sofia.ramirez@acme.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cutover buffer proposal for Acme MAP

Naomi / team —

Read the addendum and the two‑week buffer is fine from a legal perspective as long as the language gives Redwood the right to withdraw the buffer if hardware commitments change (we have limited Dedicated slots in the window). If Acme is asking for 7/22 we need to treat that as an exception request: 7/22 is outside the buffer window and will require a capacity check + a pricing exception for the extended hold period.

Marcus — can you check capacity for 7/22? If we can commit, I can draft the tighter credit language Sofia requested and sign off quickly. Rishi — if Marcus says capacity is constrained, we should outline a short credit (two weeks free + prorated hold fee) and route to finance.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, execs@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Acme close date extension request (impact + ask)

Team / Execs —

Following Sofia's note, Acme is formally requesting a cutover move to 2027‑07‑22 (three weeks beyond our proposed buffer). This is a material exception relative to the MAP and our current capacity plan. Quick impact summary and proposed next steps: 

Impact:
- Capacity: potential Dedicated GPU slot conflict for week of 7/19–7/25; Marcus to confirm availability.
- Revenue timing: ARR recognition delay ~3 weeks; finance to note potential quarter carry.
- Risk: prolonged evaluation increases chance of scope creep; ops will need a readiness gating call one week prior.

Proposed next steps (time sensitive):
1) Marcus to confirm capacity by EOD 6/25.
2) If capacity available: offer Acme the 7/22 cutover with the original commercial terms plus an explicit, signed addendum that defines the acquisition trigger and the limited credit (two weeks of discounted overage protection) if delays are on Redwood's side. Laura to finalize legal language today.
3) If capacity NOT available: offer Acme the 7/15 date (our buffer) with a small prorated hold fee and the two‑week credit; escalate to Finance for a one‑time concession approval.

Attachments: summarized risk log (close_risk_log.xlsx) and the latest draft of the MAP addendum (Acme_MAP_v2.pdf). I copied the proposed DocuSign link for the addendum.

As this touches capacity and finance timing, I recommend an immediate 20‑minute standup if Marcus reports any slot conflicts.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachment stubs: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf, close_risk_log.xlsx, docusign_acme_quote.url
